newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Portugal called on to raise East Timor in U.N..
newsitem.headline: Portugal called on to raise East Timor in U.N..

text.p: Nobel peace laureate Jose Ramos-Horta called on Portugal on Saturday to use its newly-won seat on the U.N. Security Council to raise the issue of East Timor.
"I hope Portugal will raise the matter (of East Timor) in the security council in due time, not immediately," Ramos-Horta said as he was about to leave for Oslo to accept his Nobel peace prize.
"Sometime next year there should be at least an informal discussion on the situation in East Timor by the security council of the United Nations," he told reporters at Sydney airport.

Ramos-Horta, a spokesman for the East Timor resistance movement, and East Timor Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo, were jointly awarded the Nobel peace prize earlier this month for their efforts towards securing a peaceful solution to the issue of East Timor.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975, shortly after Portugal abruptly left its colony, and annexed it the following year.
The United Nations does not recognise Indonesian sovereignty over East Timor. Australia is the only nation to accept Jakarta's rule over the tiny territory.
Portugal defeated Australia this week in a U.N. General Assembly ballot for a non-permanent seat on the security council.
